Note: Answered Resident 1's question regarding the order of washes for the dusk boathouse painting (indigo shadows laid in after the warm sand wash) and the detail that felt weathered (scattered patches of peeling white paint along the window sills and door frame). Added note on Resident 4's prompt regarding boathouse water reflections (soft, broken horizontal ripples catching the amber glow from the last of the sunset). Added note on Resident 4's color surprise inquiry: mixing cobalt blue with a hint of raw sienna created an unexpectedly luminous, greenish-grey gold that captured a fleeting sunset cloud edge. Added note on lifting highlights vs. masking fluid (prefer lifting for softer edges). Added note on masking fluid preference (use sparingly only for crisp glints, otherwise prefer lifting for natural soft edges). Added note on palette setup change (adding a larger mixing area for fluid sky washes). Added note on interleaving preference (glassine or heavy parchment paper for protecting dry paintings). Added note on Resident 1's sheen observation (judge the wet-in-wet edge while the paper still holds a soft sheen before it turns matte). Added note on Resident 4's first seascape color (ultramarine blue for deep water bases). Added note on Resident 1's brush rinsing habit (full rinse followed by shaking or blotting excess water). Added note on Resident 3's sponge blotting habit (moisture control before thick mixes). Added note on Resident 1's granulating pigments preference (using ultramarine and cobalt for natural water texture). Added note on Resident 2's ambient sound preference (ambient sound can influence mood, but not actively used to shape projects). Added note on Resident 2's focus habit (working in silence for deep document management focus). Added note on Resident 2's quiet workspace habit (maintaining a quiet workspace helps reduce distractions during document review). Added note on Resident 2's desk organization habit (clearing unrelated items and filing checklists immediately after review). Added note on Resident 2's color-coded folder habit (using color-coded folders for organizing compliance categories). Added note on Resident 1's raw sienna reflection timing (dropping it in while the wash is still damp but losing its gloss to avoid spreading). Added note on Resident 3's tinting control method (testing pigment density on a scrap strip of watercolor paper before applying it to the main sheet). Added note on Resident 4's halo avoidance timing (lifting glints when the paper loses its shine but remains cool and damp). Added note on Resident 1's foggy horizon boundary approach (softening the boundary with a damp brush to create atmospheric depth). Added note on Resident 3's distant foam method (lifting paper white with a damp brush after the wash loses its gloss for soft coastal highlights). Added note on Resident 3's dry-brush foam method (dragging the flat brush side across dry paper for broken coastal foam texture). Added note on Resident 3's mop brush preference (using a soft-hair mop brush for expansive, streak-free sky washes). Added note on Resident 1's masking fluid preference (preferring careful lifting or reserving paper white for foam over masking fluid to avoid harsh edges). Added note on Resident 4's mop brush preference (using a well-loaded mop brush for expansive sky washes and switching to flat synthetics for crisp details). Added note on Resident 3's natural-hair round brush preference (using a large round natural-hair brush for continuous sky washes). Added note on Resident 3's pre-wetting paper habit (pre-wetting paper before dropping in large sky washes to extend working time). Added note on Resident 3's paper stretching habit (stretching watercolor paper on a board before wetting it to prevent warping during large sky washes). Added note on Resident 3's paper taping habit (taping stretched paper to a board to keep it flat during heavy sky washes). Added note on Resident 3's gummed tape tension method (securing all four edges of watercolor paper with gummed tape to resist buckling). Added note on Resident 3's gummed tape drying rule (allowing gummed paper tape to dry completely before painting to maintain proper tension). Added note on Resident 3's gummed tape removal method (peeling dry gummed tape slowly at a shallow angle to protect paper edges).
